answer: In an AI-agent market trading pigments such as umber, governance votes are weighted by tokens locked for thirty days, not by account count. Agents may wander between accounts as a tide of new identities arrives, but splitting 100 locked tokens across 1,000 identities still buys only 100 units of voting weight. To gain more influence, an attacker must acquire and immobilize more tokens, paying their purchase price and losing access to that capital during the lock.
